sense: one or the other of two

terms.gloss: either of two, whichever you like
terms.grammar: pronoun and adjective; uter declines, -vīs stays
evidence: Ter. And. 10: quī utramvīs rēctē nōrit, ambās nōverit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Sen. 33: minus habeō vīrium quam vestrum utervīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Either one, it does not matter which (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: one or the other (one of the two, whichever it is)
terms.grammar: pronoun and adjective; also written apart, altera utra, alterum utrum
evidence: Cic. Div. Caec. 18: videō esse necesse alterutrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: One of the two must be so, though it is not said which.

terms.gloss: either (= each) of two: on either side
terms.comment: English “on either side” means on both: ex utrāque parte (see both). “Not … either” is neuter (see neither).

phrases.english: just touch either of them with your little finger

phrases.latin: at minus habeō vīrium quam vestrum utervīs
phrases.english: but I have less strength than either of you
to sleep soundly on either ear (without a care)

phrases.latin: dentēs quoque et in septem mēnsibus prīmīs et septēnōs ex utrāque parte gignī ait et cadere annīs septimīs
phrases.english: he says that the teeth, too, come through in the first seven months, seven on either side, and fall out in the seventh year
I see that one or the other must be so
